PLANNING.corridor_min.decision: Client decision 2026-09-25: use 900 mm. Mitton's 914 mm is 36 in converted; the two differ by 14 mm (1.6 %), so they are treated as the same recommendation (close-values policy, docs/guidance/README.md). Applying AD M's hall width to routes inside rooms is this decision, not AD M's own scope.

PLANNING.corridor_min.note: hall and landing width in an M4(2) dwelling; the rule's privacy test is qualitative (Alexander 127)

DOOR-01.decision: Restructured 2026-09-25 from Neufert room-type widths (unverified) to AD M Table 2.1. A door between two rooms is read as approached from the narrower room (the table names corridors; this reading is ours). The WC-specific 700 mm had no source and is dropped: AD M applies Table 2.1 to every door except cupboards and additional en-suites.

PLANNING.daylight_ratio.decision: Far-values policy 2026-09-25: the legacy 1/8 (12.5 %) was attributed to Neufert but is not in the held 1980 edition; the IRC 8 % is a legal minimum. LIGHT-01 is a minimum-glazing screen; daylight adequacy is judged by SLL minimum ADF (verified cards).

SAN-01.note: Presence rule, no number. Re-sourced 2026-09-25 from the unverified Neufert citation to AD G 4.8 / M4(1) and 5.6.
